criterion: every model-facing wording exposes the comparison direction of the predicate that scores it, either by naming an operator from the registered direction lexicon or by a construction registered as entailing one and admissible for that operator. A wording that gives only a target quantity fails. An awkward-but-unambiguous wording does not block and is recorded rather than fixed: changing a live wording invalidates every measurement taken under it (§10.7 A')

requirement_verb.derivation: a requirement verb is a necessity operator over the counted feature: an answer that needs q of something still needs q of it when it has more, so `necessary(S = q)` and `S >= q` select the same answers. The converse reading, `S == q`, would require the verb to forbid a further occurrence, and no requirement verb does: `needs at most` is a contradiction, not a redundancy
